items.stem: What does `use strict;` enforce in a Perl program?

options.text: It requires variables to be declared and forbids risky constructs like symbolic references
options.rationale: Correct: strict catches undeclared variables and unsafe references at compile time.

options.text: It makes the program run faster
options.rationale: strict is about correctness, not speed.
strict has no effect on regex availability.

options.text: It forces all variables to be global
options.rationale: strict encourages lexical (my) variables, the opposite of globals.

items.explanation: Correct: strict catches undeclared variables and unsafe references at compile time.

items.stem: Which statements about Perl context are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: An array evaluated in scalar context yields its element count
options.rationale: Correct: scalar context on an array gives its length.

options.text: The same expression can behave differently in list vs scalar context
options.rationale: Correct: context determines what many Perl operations return.

options.text: A hash in list context returns only its keys
options.rationale: In list context a hash returns key/value pairs, not keys alone.

options.text: Context never affects the return value of a function
options.rationale: Many functions explicitly change behaviour based on context (e.g. wantarray).

items.explanation: Correct: scalar context on an array gives its length.; Correct: context determines what many Perl operations return.

items.stem: In a Perl regex, how do you make the quantifier in `.*` match as little as possible?

options.text: Append a `?` to make it non-greedy: `.*?`
options.rationale: Correct: ? after a quantifier switches it to lazy/non-greedy matching.
! has no special quantifier meaning here.
Parentheses capture; they do not change greediness.

items.explanation: Correct: ? after a quantifier switches it to lazy/non-greedy matching.
